about.heading: About the Pnyx
about.body: The Pnyx is the hill in central Athens where the citizens' assembly gathered for over 200 years. While millions visit the Acropolis each year, the Pnyx — a short walk away — remains largely unknown. This walk tells the story of the place where democracy was not just invented, but practised.

aboutTeam.heading: Who made this?
aboutTeam.body: PNYX Athens is a personal project by two friends — no company, no tour agency. We built it because we believe this hill deserves to be more than a footnote.

about.title: Why We Made the Pnyx Experience
about.photoAlt: The two creators of PNYX Athens
story: The Pnyx Experience began with a place we could barely find.

Years ago, during a university visit to Athens, four of us set out to find the hill where the Athenian assembly had once met. When we finally reached it, we found a quiet place of extraordinary importance — and almost nothing to help visitors understand what had happened there.

Athenian democracy was far from perfect. Yet what fascinates us most is the audacity of the idea at its heart: that citizens could share political power as equals and be bound by what they decided together.
Even today, it is difficult to grasp the magnitude of that achievement.
Years later, a political philosopher and a software developer turned that experience into the Pnyx Experience — an independent audio experience grounded in ancient sources and modern research.
We made it so that visitors to the Pnyx would not merely find it, but understand what happened here — and feel the audacity of the idea that citizens can decide on shared matters for themselves.

stop1.title: Welcome to the Pnyx
stop1.description: Begin your visit on the hill where Athenian citizens gathered to govern their city and democracy came to life.

stop2.title: Why Almost Everyone Misses the Pnyx
stop2.description: Discover why this quiet hill is often overlooked, even though one of history’s most important political experiments took shape here.

stop3.title: Why This Place Matters
stop3.description: See how the decisions made on the Pnyx changed Athens and left a lasting mark on political life around the world.

stop4.title: When Athenians Gathered Here to Govern
stop4.description: Hear how thousands of citizens met in the Assembly to debate, vote and decide questions of war, law and public life.

stop5.title: How Athenians Shared Power
stop5.description: Explore the offices, councils, courts and use of selection by lot through which Athenians distributed political authority.

stop6.title: What It Meant to Be a Citizen
stop6.description: Learn about the rights, duties and exclusions that defined citizenship in democratic Athens.

stop7.title: When Athens Laughed at Itself
stop7.description: Discover how comedy mocked politicians, challenged public figures and gave Athens a way to examine its own democracy.

stop8.title: Dragged to Democracy
stop8.description: Meet the reluctant citizens who could be marked with a red-stained rope and driven toward the Assembly.

stop9.title: How Athens Became a Democracy
stop9.description: Follow the reforms and conflicts that gradually transferred political power from aristocrats to Athenian citizens.

stop10.title: Pericles the Onion-Head
stop10.description: Hear how comic poets ridiculed even the powerful Pericles by comparing the shape of his head to an onion.

stop11.title: The Sausage Seller and Demos
stop11.description: Enter Aristophanes’ comedy in which a sausage seller competes to win over Demos, the personification of the Athenian people.

stop12.title: The Play That Made Athens Cry
stop12.description: Discover why a tragedy about the fall of Miletus moved its Athenian audience to tears—and brought its author a fine.

stop13.title: The Night Socrates Drank Everyone Under the Table
stop13.description: Join the famous banquet where Socrates outlasted every other guest and walked away at dawn as composed as ever.

stop14.title: When Persia Asked “Who Are the Athenians?”
stop14.description: Hear how an unfamiliar Greek city drew the attention of the Persian Empire and stepped onto the stage of world history.

sections.heading: 1. Who we are
paragraphs: PNYX Athens is an independent educational project and the controller of the information described below. For this test phase, use the contact details on the Contact page.

sections.heading: 2. What we collect
paragraphs: Test survey: We store the answers you choose to submit and the submission time. The current survey does not collect your email address, listening progress, browser details, screen size or a session identifier.
Email updates: If you subscribe, we store your email address, consent, signup source and signup time.

Minimal analytics: We record events such as page views, audio starts and completions, language choice, directions clicks and contribution interactions. These records contain the page, event type, story identifier where relevant and limited event metadata. We do not assign an analytics user identifier or use advertising trackers.

sections.heading: 3. Browser storage
paragraphs: Your browser stores your language and theme preferences, audio progress, survey draft and a local marker after survey submission. This information stays on your device and is not sent with the anonymous test survey.

sections.heading: 4. Why we use information
paragraphs: We use survey answers and minimal analytics to test and improve PNYX. We use email addresses only to send updates requested by the subscriber. We do not sell or rent this information.

sections.heading: 5. Processor and retention
paragraphs: Application data is stored with Supabase, which processes it on our behalf. Survey submissions and analytics events are deleted after 12 months. Email signup data is kept until you unsubscribe or request deletion.

sections.heading: 6. Your rights
paragraphs: Where data protection law applies, you may request access, correction, deletion, restriction or objection and may complain to your data protection authority. Use the Contact page for requests. This test policy must be reviewed with final controller and contact details before public launch.

sections.heading: 1. Nature of this service
paragraphs: PNYX Athens is a self-guided educational audio walk for independent visitors. It is not an official guided tour, not a licensed tourist guide service, and it is not affiliated with the Hellenic Ministry of Culture, the City of Athens, or any official archaeological authority.

sections.heading: 2. Visitor responsibility
paragraphs: By using this walk, you confirm that you are visiting the Pnyx independently and at your own risk. You are responsible for your own safety, including checking weather conditions, wearing appropriate footwear, carrying water, and following all signs and regulations at the site.

sections.heading: 3. Accuracy of content
paragraphs: The historical information in this walk is provided for educational purposes. While we aim for accuracy, we make no warranty as to the completeness or correctness of the content. For authoritative information, consult academic sources or the official Hellenic Ministry of Culture.

sections.heading: 4. Limitation of liability
paragraphs: PNYX Athens accepts no liability for any injury, loss, or damage that occurs during your visit to the Pnyx or as a result of following this walk. Use this service at your own discretion.

sections.heading: 5. Intellectual property
paragraphs: The content of this walk, including text and audio, is the property of PNYX Athens. You may not reproduce or distribute it without permission. Historical facts in the public domain are not claimed as proprietary.

sections.heading: 6. Changes to terms
paragraphs: We may update these terms from time to time. Continued use of the service after changes constitutes acceptance of the revised terms.

sectionsBeforeTable.heading: Cookie and browser storage notice
paragraphs: This site does not use advertising or third-party analytics cookies. It uses browser storage for language, theme, audio progress, survey drafts and a local submitted marker.

sectionsAfterTable.heading: Cookie and browser storage notice
paragraphs: Visitors are not given an analytics cookie. Minimal analytics is stored as separate server-side events without a visitor identifier.
You can clear local PNYX preferences and progress through your browser settings. Doing so resets language, theme, listening progress and local survey state.
